analysis:
Documentation-only changes. docs/provider/cli-reference.md changes the date, adds drain-without-acknowledgement text (around head line 443-447, visible only in the patch excerpt) and adds a coordinator handshake deadline row (head line 1943). docs/reference/protocol-messages.md changes the date and adds a note at head lines 170-174 that a lifecycle drain completes without a coordinator acknowledgement when no session is registered. No executable code, wire format, or enforced control is changed in the supplied evidence.

Relevant threat models: TB-002 (coordinator/provider WebSocket), T-010 (cancellation and availability), T-053 (stale authorization across connection changes), T-057 (availability). The documented drain behavior is narrow: it applies only when no work remains and no registered session exists, while a registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. The text therefore does not claim to weaken the acknowledgement requirement or the admission fencing for a registered session. The handshake row documents a 30s deadline with cancel and retry under the existing reconnect backoff, which is an availability-positive statement.

Unverified contract: the actual behavior in ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift (performLifecycleDrain) and CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift is not supplied. A next pass should confirm that 'no registered session' cannot be reached while the coordinator still considers the provider active or admitting work, for example during a reconnect race, since that would allow a drain to complete and an update to proceed with in-flight work. Because this is a documentation-only claim about unseen code, I record it as a question rather than a finding.

The unchanged remainder of cli-reference.md (units 10 and 11) was skimmed. It contains no new security-relevant changes beyond the patch hunks. Pre-existing content and the cache T-041 definitions are unchanged by this PR.
